const { getTextTransformer } = require('./solution');
if (getTextTransformer('constructor') !== getTextTransformer('plain')) throw new Error('Unknown constructor name resolved inherited property instead of plain transformer');

prompt.text:
Implement a CommonJS module exporting exactly `{ getTextTransformer }`.

`getTextTransformer(name)` returns one of four reusable transformation functions:

- `"plain"`: returns its input unchanged.
- `"upper"`: converts the input to uppercase.
- `"snake"`: trims the input, replaces each non-empty run of whitespace with `_`, and lowercases it.
- `"reverse"`: reverses Unicode code points using `Array.from`.

Transformer lookup must trim `name` and compare it case-insensitively. An unknown name, an empty or whitespace-only name, or a non-string name must return the `plain` transformer. Every returned transformer must throw `TypeError` when invoked with a non-string value. The function must not mutate any input, and separate lookups for aliases differing only by case or surrounding whitespace must return the same function object.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.
